relationship-analytics.title: Relationship analytics overview – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
relationship-analytics.notes: Relationship analytics in Dynamics 365 Sales takes the activity history between a seller and a contact or account and turns it into KPIs. Such KPIs exist for contacts, accounts, opportunities and leads, and they are shown graphically so sellers and sales managers can see which relationships need care and which indicators could improve. The basic tier is available out of the box and draws on emails and appointments sent and received in Dynamics 365, with widgets such as a summary, most contacted, customer interactions, email engagement and email sent/received ratio. The enhanced tier adds widgets like relationship health, hourly investment, similar won deals and response time. It requires a suitable Dynamics 365 Sales license plus an administrator who enables and configures relationship intelligence. Response time depends on a connection to Exchange Online, and similar won deals applies only to opportunities. Email engagement counts only emails that are tracked. The page also warns that the feature must not be used for decisions about employment, pay or similar employee rights, and customers remain responsible for lawful use.

relationship-intelligence.title: Relationship intelligence overview – Dynamics 365 Sales – Microsoft Learn
relationship-intelligence.notes: Relationship intelligence in Dynamics 365 Sales helps sales teams keep track of customer relationships by surfacing insight into relationship health, who knows whom and related topics. It is built on how salespeople interact with their customers, and its purpose is to monitor the health and risk of relationships and to spot customers that need attention. One component, relationship analytics and health, presents KPIs and activity trends for contacts, opportunities, leads and accounts, using interaction data from Dynamics 365 and Microsoft Exchange. It appears on opportunity forms, list views and charts. The second component, who knows whom, suggests colleagues who know a lead and lets the seller ask them by email for an introduction. This is based on email interactions and meetings in the organization's Exchange environment. Contacts or leads outside the Exchange organization can be queried, while internal users only in some cases. The page lists no licenses or prices and points to separate articles for configuring each component.

request-for-information-action.title: Request for information in agent flows – Microsoft Copilot Studio – Microsoft Learn
request-for-information-action.notes: The request for information action lets an agent flow pause, collect input from named human reviewers and use the answers in later steps. It is found under the human review category in the flow designer and needs a flow with a trigger that has been published before testing. The required fields are a title that becomes the email subject, a message with the request text, and an assigned-to list of recipients. When several recipients are listed, only the response of the first person to answer is processed. Inputs can be text, yes/no, email, number or date, and fields can be made optional and given placeholder text. Single-select and multi-select choices are possible only for text inputs. Each input produces a parameter that later actions, such as an AI approval, can use as dynamic content. Requests are currently sent only through Outlook and cannot go to users outside the tenant. A known issue is that outputs may be wrapped in double curly braces, which can be avoided by naming inputs without spaces. The page does not state licensing requirements.

restricted-content-discovery.title: Restricted content discovery – SharePoint in Microsoft 365 – Microsoft Learn
restricted-content-discovery.notes: Restricted content discovery is a site-level setting for SharePoint that limits how easily a site's content, including recently edited files, can be found through organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot answers. It is meant as a temporary governance control that buys time to review permissions while Copilot rollout continues. Admins turn it on in the SharePoint admin center or with the Set-SPOSite cmdlet, and affected sites show a restricted label. The setting also hides AI entry points on those sites, such as the Copilot button and creating pages with AI. Management can be delegated to site admins, who must then give a reason, and changes are recorded in the Microsoft Purview audit log. It requires a Microsoft Copilot license and SharePoint Advanced Management. It does not change permissions, does not remove content from the search index, and leaves eDiscovery and auto-labeling working. It applies to SharePoint sites only, not OneDrive. Typical targets are sites at risk of oversharing, such as finance or HR sites. Heavy use can reduce the completeness of search and Copilot results.

routing-diagnostics.title: View unified routing diagnostics – Dynamics 365 Customer Service – Microsoft Learn
routing-diagnostics.notes: Routing diagnostics in Dynamics 365 Customer Service gives a detailed view of each routed record so that problems in classifying and assigning work items can be investigated. Unified routing sends a work item to the most suitable service representative or queue based on skills and related entities. The diagnostics page lists columns such as work item, routing status, duration, work stream, queue, routed agent and rule hit policy. Each item is followed through the stages intake, classification, route to queue and assignment. Intake applies only to record routing, classification shows which rulesets and machine learning models ran, and assignment shows prioritization, the assignment method, capacity, presence, skills and an attempt trace. Admins switch it on from the routing area of the Copilot Service admin center, and data is kept in Dataverse. Routed records use more storage than other work item types, and information can appear with a delay. Some model details are marked as preview. The page states that the feature is deprecated and does not name specific license requirements.

runbook.title: Azure Automation runbook types – Microsoft Learn
runbook.notes: The page describes the runbook types in the process automation feature of Azure Automation rather than defining the term formally. The types are PowerShell, PowerShell Workflow, Python, Graphical and Graphical PowerShell Workflow. PowerShell and Python are the recommended text-based types, and the PowerShell runtime version is selected per runbook. Runbooks can run in Azure or on hybrid runbook workers, which can be Windows or Linux machines. Text runbooks can be edited in the portal or written offline and imported, while graphical runbooks can be edited only in the portal, although they can be exported and imported into other automation accounts. PowerShell Workflow adds checkpoints and parallel processing but must be compiled before running, so it starts more slowly and is not available on Linux hybrid workers. Python runbooks can use Python libraries, with modules supplied as wheel files, and do not support webhooks. Graphical runbooks cannot be converted to text types or digitally signed. Some PowerShell 7 limitations apply, such as no workflows and no signed runbooks. Runbooks can also call other runbooks as children, with restrictions across types.

saas-fulfillment-apis.title: SaaS fulfillment APIs – Partner Center – Microsoft Learn
saas-fulfillment-apis.notes: The SaaS fulfillment APIs let publishers, meaning independent software vendors, sell their software-as-a-service applications through Microsoft's commercial marketplace. They keep the subscription state on the publisher side in step with Microsoft and cover direct, partner-led and field-led sales channels. Integrating them is required before a transactable SaaS offer or a free trial can be created and published in Partner Center. The documented flows include the landing page flow that tells the publisher about a purchase, activation, optional automatic activation, updates to plan or license count, and suspend and reinstate when a payment method is invalid. Webhooks report changes and cancellations triggered on the Microsoft side. Cancellation integration is optional because customers can cancel there as well. Prerequisites are registering the application as a Microsoft Entra application and using service-to-service authentication, with calls made only from the publisher's backend and not from web pages. Version 2 is the recommended version, and version 1 is deprecated and no longer documented. For reseller purchases through a cloud solution provider, the publisher does not have to implement the flows differently.

saga-pattern.title: Saga design pattern – Azure Architecture Center – Microsoft Learn
saga-pattern.notes: The saga pattern keeps data consistent across several services by running a sequence of local transactions. Each service commits its own work in its own database and triggers the next step through an event or message. If a step fails, compensating transactions reverse the effects of the steps already completed. It serves as an alternative to two-phase commit in distributed systems where ACID guarantees do not span multiple databases. The page separates compensable transactions, a pivot transaction that marks the point of no return, and retryable transactions that follow it and must be idempotent. Sagas can be coordinated by choreography, where services exchange events without a central controller, or by orchestration, where a central orchestrator tracks task state and handles failures. Choreography is simple but can become hard to follow and risks cyclic dependencies, while orchestration suits complex workflows but adds coordination effort. Drawbacks include a different mental model, harder debugging, compensations that may themselves fail, and anomalies such as lost updates and dirty reads because sagas lack isolation. Countermeasures include semantic locks and versioning.
